title_en: Nurture: a Necessity and a Method
body_ar: للتربية أهمية كبرى في حياة المسلم بجوانبها الثلاثة: العقلي، والبدني، والروحي، وهي ضرورية أيضاً لمن أراد أن ينتقل من الجهل إلى العلم، ومن الضعف إلى القوة، ومن الخلق السيئ إلى الخلق الحسن. ومن أعظم ما يعين على التربية قراءة سير السلف والخلف ممن ضربوا أروع الأمثلة في التربية الحسنة. أهمية التربية في حياة المسلم: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وصلى الله وسلم على نبينا محمد وعلى آله وأصحابه أجمعين، ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. أما بعد: فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى خلق الإنسان من ضعف، وجعله قابلاً للنمو والتطور، وآتاه وسائل ذلك النمو والتطور، فيسر له سبل الهدى، وأعانه على ذلك بما آتاه من الجوارح المعينة على التدبر في آيات الله المسطورة والمنظورة ليزداد بذلك إيماناً ويقيناً؛ وليزداد في أخلاقه وفي سلوكه وفي أعماله كلها...
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* Nurture has the greatest importance in the life of a Muslim, in its three aspects: the intellectual, the bodily and the spiritual. It is also necessary for whoever wishes to pass from ignorance to knowledge, from weakness to strength, and from bad character to good character. Among the greatest aids to nurture is the reading of the lives of the early and the later generations, of those who set the finest examples of good nurture.

## The importance of nurture in the life of a Muslim

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. May God bless and grant peace to our Prophet Muhammad, and to his family and all his Companions, and to all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. To proceed:

God, glorified and exalted is He, created the human being out of weakness and made him capable of growth and development, and gave him the means of that growth and development. He made the paths of guidance easy for him, and aided him in that by the bodily faculties He gave him, which assist in pondering God's signs, both those written down and those seen, so that by this he might increase in faith and in certainty, and increase in his character, in his conduct and in all his deeds...

flags.note: tarbiyah spans upbringing, moral formation and education, and the record uses it across all three of the aspects it names — intellectual, bodily and spiritual — so no narrower English word will carry it. 'Nurture' is used consistently so that a reviewer can substitute one word throughout. Not in the glossary; it recurs across the corpus and should be settled.

translator_notes: One of a run of thirteen records, IDs 688-700, all uploaded on 5 and 8-9 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/c-a-* series. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lessons were delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.
'السلف والخلف' is rendered 'the early and the later generations' rather than 'the Salaf and the Khalaf', which in English carries the names of modern positions the Arabic does not invoke here.
No ruling term appears anywhere in the record.
